top_categories.workout_context: 51ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Gdynia. Train it until it feels boring.
78 miles on rolling Kashubian hinterland burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Gdynia's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
At Gran Fondo Gdynia, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Gran Fondo Gdynia's rolling Kashubian hinterland forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 78 miles.
When someone attacks on rolling Kashubian hinterland, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,003ft of climbing on rolling Kashubian hinterland does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on rolling Kashubian hinterland demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Base fitness for Gran Fondo Gdynia. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
76–85% FTP for extended efforts. At Gran Fondo Gdynia, tempo is the floor you'll live on. Make it feel easy.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Gdynia’s 78 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, G Spot, and Durability to prepare you for 78 miles of rolling kashubian hinterland in Gdynia, Poland (start/finish ul. Olimpijska, loop through Wejherowo/Kartuzy Kashubian hinterland).
